update description: The Specify Needs phase is now supported by automated and AI-powered processes for synthesizing stakeholder inputs, analyzing options, and drafting business cases. Routine tasks are minimized for manual involvement; staff focus on higher-value interpretation, establishing priorities, and strategic decision-making. Staff must pivot from manual investigation to oversight, contextualization, and expert validation of AI-driven inputs.
interdependencies: Cascades into all subsequent process phases, especially design, analysis, and evaluation, as needs specification guides priorities throughout statistical lifecycle.
impact reasoning: For the EC-02 (Economist/Sociologist 2) position, involvement in needs specification shifts from hands-on manual analysis (e.g., environmental scanning, direct synthesis of all feedback) to overseeing, interpreting, and validating AI-synthesized feedback and stakeholder needs. The role becomes more about expert judgment, critical appraisal of automated outputs, and ensuring that nuanced or emergent issues are not missed by AI tools. Recommendations and feedback developed by the EC-02 will reference, validate, and, if necessary, challenge or supplement AI-identified needs.

gaps.justification: Current expectations assume manual synthesis/preparation; future role requires ability to critically review AI-generated inputs, recognize limitations/gaps, and contextualize automated findings.
gaps.name: AI-enabled Analysis Review
gaps.description: Ability to interpret, validate, and provide expert input on AI- or automation-generated needs analyses, material, and business case recommendations.

gaps.description: Knowledge of how AI generates, detects, or highlights statistical trends, including its potential blind spots, bias, or error types, to inform when expert override or supplementation is required.

update description: AI and automated tools continuously aggregate and analyze information requests, environmental signals, and respondent feedback—structuring and benchmarking needs for statistics. Staff now interpret context, assess the significance of AI-identified needs, and handle complex/emerging requirements.
interdependencies: Related to GSBPM 1 (Specify needs); influences subsequent workflow in needs validation, process design, and later analytic/evaluation stages.
impact reasoning: For the EC-02 position, the investigative component of identifying user/statistical needs is no longer a mainly manual task. Instead, the EC-02 will interact primarily with AI-generated syntheses of needs input (e.g., user requests, feedback, international benchmarks). Their role becomes more evaluative and interpretive: validating the relevance, accuracy, and completeness of AI-flagged needs, resolving ambiguous, context-dependent, or emergent issues that AI may not surface, and providing nuanced recommendations for action. Their attention is shifted toward high-value exceptions and insight, rather than broad data collection or routine scanning.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: Identifies statistical trends and developments.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This task now starts with AI-generated outputs (trend lists, priority signals, benchmarks from external sources). The EC-02 evaluates, contextualizes, and refines these outputs for program decision-making.

gaps.description: Ability to review, critique, and contextualize needs/trends identified by AI tools, and to intervene where additional data, nuance, or subject-matter assessment is required.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Feedback and recommendations are increasingly based on synthesis of automated needs analysis and benchmarking, requiring the EC-02 to specialize in interpreting, qualifying, and supplementing automated needs assessments for survey/method change proposals.

gaps.justification: Gap arises because feedback is no longer based primarily on manual investigation/review but on automated, sometimes opaque AI analytics.

gaps.description: Skill in interrogating, validating, and integrating AI-generated findings when forming constructive feedback, proposals, and recommendations.

gaps.justification: Requires an ability to operate flexibly between automated insight and higher-level analytic thinking, with comfort in AI oversight and intervention.

gaps.description: Ability to dynamically integrate automated research/analysis outputs with expert-driven inquiry, especially when AI signals limitations in emerging/complex needs.

update description: Consulting with stakeholders and confirming user needs is now largely organized and synthesized by automated/AI-supported systems, which aggregate and highlight stakeholder input, patterns, and evolving requirements over time. Economist/Sociologist 2 roles shift to oversight, prioritization, context-aware judgment, and direct engagement only for nuanced, ambiguous, or high-stakes negotiation cases.
interdependencies: Related to GSBPM 1.1 (Identify needs) and GSBPM 1 (Specify needs). Strongly influences requirements gathering, system design, and downstream analytic approaches.
impact reasoning: EC-02's involvement pivots from manual collection and collation of user requirements to a supervision and interpretive role. Primary contributions are critical review of AI-generated summaries, direct intervention in resolving subtleties missed by AI, and leadership (even under supervision) in setting prioritization schemas or escalation for complex, contentious, or contextual issues. The EC-02 must be able to interrogate and interpret insights surfaced algorithmically, focusing effort on ensuring requirements are interpreted accurately and user needs are authentically reflected.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Provision of data/assistance is now mediated by an AI-driven consultation interface (e.g., user feedback synthesis, chatbots, summary dashboards). EC-02 is responsible for overseeing the quality of support, interpreting priority cases, and stepping in for user support in ambiguous or complex scenarios.

gaps.justification: Move from manual user support/data provision to oversight of AI-moderated communication, plus intervention in exception/priority cases.
gaps.name: Supervision of AI-mediated User Consultation
gaps.description: Ability to assess quality, interpret, and escalate user needs and feedback synthesized by automated systems, with direct user engagement as needed for complex or high-priority issues.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Liaison now includes interpreting requirements identified via AI automation, validating accuracy and completeness, and negotiating contextual details with users and subject matter experts only for cases requiring expert input. Routine translation/negotiation of requirements is automated except for nuanced or complex cases.

gaps.justification: Skill needs shift from basic liaison and translation of requirements to critical validation of AI-generated specifications and skilled negotiation over ambiguities or priorities.
gaps.name: AI-augmented Stakeholder Liaison
gaps.description: Skill in validating and contextualizing AI-aggregated requirements, prioritizing them, and negotiating procedural adjustments or clarifications in partnership with automation outputs.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Contextual expertise is still vital, but its use refocuses on validating, clarifying, and supplementing needs assessments automatically surfaced by AI tools—ensuring human insight fills automation gaps and helps set priorities.

gaps.justification: Requires blending domain/contextual expertise with understanding of automated consultation systems and how/where they may misinterpret or overlook important contextual details.
gaps.name: Expert-AI Collaboration in Needs Confirmation
gaps.description: Knowledge of where human intervention is needed to supplement, confirm, or correct AI-synthesized needs and requirements based on deep contextual program understanding.

update description: AI and automation now generate draft statistical output objectives and candidate quality measures by analyzing user requirements, past practice, legal frameworks, and resource limits. EC-02 roles shift from basic assembly/suggestion to expert oversight, strategic alignment, and compliance adjudication—focusing on the final judgment about appropriateness and compliance rather than routine formulation.
interdependencies: Upstream dependence on GSBPM 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs); downstream impact on all phases involving standards compliance, strategic alignment, and performance monitoring.
impact reasoning: EC-02 staff engage less in collecting the raw inputs needed to set output objectives and more in evaluating, refining, and approving AI-generated proposals. This requires abilities in comparing AI-produced drafts with legal constraints, historical standards, and program strategy. Human review ensures AI-synthesized objectives are not only technically correct but also contextually, legally, and ethically robust. EC-02 becomes a quality and compliance filter, and an escalation point for trade-off decisions.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Analysis and preparation of analytical material now starts from AI/automation-generated objectives (drafts, proposed measures), which the EC-02 validates for compliance, completeness, and contextual appropriateness.

gaps.justification: Gap is between current manual drafting versus critical appraisal/validation role for AI-generated objectives and documentation.

gaps.description: Ability to critically assess and refine AI-generated output objectives and accompanying quality measures for compliance with legal frameworks, organizational strategy, and user needs.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Feedback and recommendations for objectives focus on strategic and compliance issues detected in AI-generated material, moving staff up the value chain toward final approval and risk management.

gaps.justification: Now requires expert judgment regarding the sufficiency of automated drafts and an ability to escalate/adjust issues that are not resolved in automation.

gaps.description: Ability to judge, escalate, and resolve strategic, legal, or ethical trade-offs surfaced by AI-driven proposal generation; ensure compliance and appropriateness in all analytical outputs.

update description: Identifying concepts is now supported by AI-powered synthesis of user needs and references, producing draft or preliminary conceptual frameworks for measurement. The EC-02 (as subject matter representative or supporting sponsor) is solely accountable for reviewing, specifying, and formally certifying these concepts for downstream use, ensuring accurate translation from user needs and proper documentation. Manual workload is reduced, but accountability and validation responsibilities are heightened.
interdependencies: Feeds directly into GSBPM 2.2 (Design variables) and is dependent on input quality from 1.2/1.3 (consulting needs and establishing objectives). Accountability relationship to downstream design and quality control.
impact reasoning: Where previously the EC-02 would have synthesized requirements and developed proposals largely by hand or collaborative iteration, they are now responsible for critical review and certification of AI-suggested concepts. Liaison activity evolves into high-level evaluation and finalization—ensuring chosen concepts are theoretically and statistically justifiable, and clearly resolved for handoff. The EC-02 also documents rationale for decisions, advocates for corrections if AI/automation misaligns with context, and demonstrates sole accountability in the certification record.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Preparation starts from AI pre-synthesized options for concepts. The EC-02 is responsible for detailed review, selection, refinement, and official sign-off, with increased focus on theoretical and statistical adequacy.

gaps.justification: Gap arises because staff will no longer be guided solely by precedent or collaboration; instead, they must fully understand, critique, and own the final conceptual specifications.
gaps.name: Final Concept Specification and AI Validation
gaps.description: Ability to critically evaluate AI-generated conceptual inputs, make theoretically/statistically informed selections, justify final specifications, and formally certify concepts for process use.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Liaison now requires cross-functional communication to explain, defend, and document concept certification rationale, with an emphasis on reconciling AI-driven suggestions with organizational strategy/needs and formalizing final subject-matter positions.

gaps.justification: The shift to sole accountability requires strong skills in justifying and documenting conceptual choices, including explicit rationale for selecting/rejecting AI-proposed concepts.

update description: This sub-process now requires formal, systematic, and prioritized exploration of all existing data and administrative/alternative sources before survey collection is considered. The subject matter sponsor (supported by a center of expertise) holds sole accountability for certifying that all data avenues have been fully explored and suitability is rigorously assessed. The EC-02 must evaluate automated/AI-summarized outputs related to data availability, oversee documentation, participate in collaborative acquisition efforts, and officially certify adequacy and suitability.
interdependencies: Feeds into survey design if no sufficient data sources are found; strong links to downstream phases (design, collection) and to GSBPM concepts of certification, documentary rigor, and legal compliance.
impact reasoning: For the EC-02 role, traditional exploratory or ad hoc search for data sources is mostly replaced with systematic, automation-supported sweeps of all available data holdings. Duties now focus on critical evaluation of AI/tool-generated overviews—certifying, documenting, and, where needed, negotiating with a center of expertise for non-survey data sourcing, as well as updating or challenging legal/operational agreements. The EC-02 role becomes one of oversight and formal responsibility, requiring both substantive knowledge and process documentation rigor.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: EC-02 reviews and certifies AI-aggregated data inventories/availability analyses, ensuring analytical work only proceeds with fully vetted and documented data sources.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Assessment of data validity now necessitates the evaluation of complex, automated audits and the ability to contextualize findings, flag shortcomings, or escalate for alternative acquisition agreements.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Proposals for changes to systems shift from manual research to interpretation and improvement of systematically automated search and assessment tools, in collaboration with data acquisition experts and for strategic process direction.

update description: Business case preparation is now largely automated: AI-driven systems assemble draft sections (current state, recommendations, risk/benefit assessment, resource estimates). Staff—such as EC-02—are tasked with strategic, contextual review and with refining and substantiating AI-drafted content to fit organizational strategy and operational realities. Final submission requires expertise in recognizing gaps, validating assumptions, and ensuring the business case is defensible and actionable.
interdependencies: Heavily dependent on prior sub-processes for accurate input; downstream impact on approval and project initiation in GSBPM 2 (Design).
impact reasoning: The role for the EC-02 shifts from hands-on authoring or assembling business case materials to oversight, critical validation, and revision of drafts prepared by AI. The position's value-add focuses on expert plausibility testing, catching automation-missed nuances, clarifying risk, ensuring all options are correctly presented and assuming ownership for final, quality-controlled recommendations or scenario descriptions. This work will require critical thinking for both the substantive (statistical/economic) and process (project/strategic) dimensions of proposals.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Preparation now starts with AI-generated business case sections; EC-02 must vet content, contextualize findings, spot gaps/risks/weaknesses, and contribute to strategic alignment of final materials.

gaps.justification: Gap exists between current manual authoring/reporting skills and future need to critically review, contextualize, and supplement complex, AI-produced documentation.
gaps.name: Critical Review and Contextualization of AI-Generated Business Cases
gaps.description: Ability to identify deficiencies and articulate context, risks, and nuances in AI-prepared business case drafts. Capable of adjusting and defending proposals to satisfy oversight bodies and ensure actionability.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Now includes assessment of business case impact and appropriateness, by interpreting AI-assembled scenarios, risks, and resource estimates. EC-02 must ground these analyses in operational and contextual realities.

gaps.justification: Need for expertise in translating AI-identified impacts and assumptions into credible, defensible arguments for approval forums.
gaps.name: AI-assisted Business Case Interpretation
gaps.description: In-depth understanding of how AI-assembled business cases can miss, misrepresent or oversimplify contextual factors; ability to adjust, interpret, and justify scenarios and recommendations for an executive/governance audience.

update description: Design phase now emphasizes AI- and automation-enabled tools for drafting outputs, methods, and process specifications. All metadata and outputs are standardized, machine-actionable, and interoperable by default. The EC-02 role shifts toward the oversight, strategic review, and adaptation of automated, standards-based designs. Routine/repetitive work is greatly reduced; work now centers on ensuring methodological rigor and optimal analytic fitness.
interdependencies: Feeds all downstream phases, especially Build, Collect, and Evaluate; highly dependent on upstream specification of needs and objectives.
impact reasoning: Instead of constructing design documents and metadata by hand, EC-02s review, refine, and adapt automated products for alignment with program requirements, analytic utility, and user needs. Judgment is especially needed around selection or customization of standards, and in evaluating interoperability and metadata sufficiency from a subject-matter perspective. Their expertise ensures that the digital-first approach doesn't bypass essential nuance or create analytic obstacles.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Preparation and analytical work now entails interpreting AI-generated design documents/specifications, confirming they are analytically suitable, and flagging or adapting areas that require subject-matter-driven revision.

gaps.description: Ability to review, adapt, and provide analytic context to AI- and automation-generated design specifications, ensuring alignment with analytic objectives and stakeholder requirements.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Feedback and recommendations are now iterative responses to digital design elements and automated process outputs, requiring the EC-02 to participate in calibration and innovation rather than base-level construction.

gaps.justification: Where feedback was previously based on lived/manual design process experience, future feedback requires understanding and shaping automation and digital workflows.
gaps.name: Digital Workflow Calibration and Innovation
gaps.description: Skill in identifying, adapting, and documenting improvements or innovations within AI/automation-based design processes to better support analytic and operational objectives.

The role becomes one of quality assurance, exception handling, and continuous methodological improvement, ensuring outputs remain robust, reproducible, and in line with emerging standards and operational requirements.

gaps.description: Ability to appraise and propose changes or improvements to AI- or digital-pipeline-implemented survey and analytic routines, ensuring auditability, compliance, and analytic fit.

Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This knowledge is now used to check for methodological and theoretical nuance that AI/automation may overlook, and to intervene when digital pipelines imply risks to analytic quality, repeatability, or compliance.

update description: All analysis of statistical outputs—drafting, validation, and commentary—is now automated and AI-powered, with modular real-time pipelines producing dashboards, write-ups, and summaries by default.
